title: The Pursuit of Happyness
synopsis: Twenty unpaid weeks, one son, and exactly nineteen other interns competing for the single job at the end. You can't afford to lose. You also can't afford to win.

nodes.text: You stand in a borrowed suit on a floor of men in real ones. Your son is in daycare you can't afford. The internship is unpaid. The job, if you win it, will change everything.

choices.text: Speak up early to be noticed
choices.consequence: Visibility is half the game. You choose to speak up early to be noticed. It opens the route to First Impression, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Stay quiet and observe everything
choices.consequence: Knowing the room beats announcing yourself. You commit to stay quiet and observe everything. By The Cold Calls, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: You ask a sharp question in the morning meeting. A senior broker raises an eyebrow — could be 'impressed,' could be 'put him on my list.' You will, for the next nineteen weeks, never know which.

choices.text: Lean into the bold version of yourself
choices.consequence: Brave is a strategy, not a feeling. You commit to lean into the bold version of yourself. By The Eviction Notice, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Dial it back and prove yourself in numbers
choices.consequence: Quiet excellence is harder to dismiss. You commit to dial it back and prove yourself in numbers. By A Lead, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: By afternoon you're on the phones, dialing strangers. Most hang up. One curses you out. You take notes on what worked. You realize you are very, very good at this. The distance between The Eviction Notice and A Lead begins with the choice between “Burn through the call list at speed” and “Pick fewer calls, go deeper with each.”

choices.text: Burn through the call list at speed
choices.consequence: Volume is its own kind of magic. You burn through the call list at speed. The decision moves you toward The Eviction Notice and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Pick fewer calls, go deeper with each
choices.consequence: Quality is a slow weapon. You commit to pick fewer calls, go deeper with each. By A Lead, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: You come home to a piece of paper taped to your door. Fourteen days. Your son shows you a drawing he made. He has not eaten anything green this week. You smile at the drawing.

choices.text: Tell him the truth in kid-sized pieces
choices.consequence: Honesty he can carry is a gift. You commit to tell him the truth in kid-sized pieces. By The Shelter Line, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Protect him from it for one more night
choices.consequence: Some weights you carry alone, by choice. You protect him from it for one more night. The decision moves you toward The Big Meeting and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: A name you cold-called actually calls back — a big one, distracted, but listening. He'll meet you in person if you can be at his office across the city tomorrow at 7 a.m. “Commit to the meeting at any cost” opens the route to The Shelter Line. “Try to reschedule to a day you can manage” changes the terms and carries you toward The Big Meeting.

choices.text: Commit to the meeting at any cost
choices.consequence: Doors open once, and not by appointment. You choose to commit to the meeting at any cost. It opens the route to The Shelter Line, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Try to reschedule to a day you can manage
choices.consequence: Sometimes the door reopens; usually not. You choose to try to reschedule to a day you can manage. It opens the route to The Big Meeting, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: You and your son stand in line for the church shelter. It rains. He holds a toy rocket. He asks if you have a plan. You say yes — quietly, because the people behind you are too close, and because saying it out loud is also how you start to believe it.

choices.text: Make sure he sees you stay calm
choices.consequence: Calm in a parent is its own kind of meal. You choose to make sure he sees you stay calm. It opens the route to Subway Bathroom, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Let him see you're scared, too
choices.consequence: Some lessons require an honest face. You commit to let him see you're scared, too. By The Rolodex, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: You make it across the city at 7 a.m. — somehow — and the prospect actually shakes your hand. Twenty minutes of his time. You can hear your own heartbeat. Begin. “Pitch hard with everything you know” draws you toward Subway Bathroom; “Listen first, then offer what fits him” leaves The Rolodex waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Pitch hard with everything you know
choices.consequence: When the door opens you do not knock politely. You pitch hard with everything you know. The decision moves you toward Subway Bathroom and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Listen first, then offer what fits him
choices.consequence: The best pitch is sometimes a question. You commit to listen first, then offer what fits him. By The Rolodex, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: There's a night when the shelter is full and you and your son sleep in a subway-station bathroom with the door wedged shut. You sing to him. You promise yourself you will never tell anyone about tonight. You will. Eventually.

choices.text: Sing him through to sleep
choices.consequence: Voice is a kind of roof. You sing him through to sleep. The decision moves you toward The Friend and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Hold him in silence so he hears your heart
choices.consequence: Some lullabies don't have words. You choose to hold him in silence so he hears your heart. It opens the route to The Bone Scanner Sale, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Your manager hands you a rolodex of names and a target. The other interns are richer, better-educated, sharper-suited. You stare at the cards. You realize you have one advantage they don't — desperation. Choose “Turn desperation into discipline” and The Friend comes into view; choose “Try to make a friend among the interns first” and the road bends toward The Bone Scanner Sale.

choices.text: Turn desperation into discipline
choices.consequence: Hunger is a tool only if you sharpen it. You choose to turn desperation into discipline. It opens the route to The Friend, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Try to make a friend among the interns first
choices.consequence: Allies inside the wall are also currency. You choose to try to make a friend among the interns first. It opens the route to The Bone Scanner Sale, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: One of the interns — Naomi, whose father is also her boss somewhere — surprises you. She doesn't pity you. She just sits beside you in the cafeteria like it's normal. You'd forgotten how that felt. The distance between Your Son's Birthday and Midterm Review begins with the choice between “Accept the friendship at face value” and “Stay polite but keep your distance.”

choices.text: Accept the friendship at face value
choices.consequence: Not everyone with money is the enemy. You choose to accept the friendship at face value. It opens the route to Your Son's Birthday, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Stay polite but keep your distance
choices.consequence: Friendship in a competition is a soft target. You commit to stay polite but keep your distance. By Midterm Review, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: You're still trying to sell the medical scanners you bought before the internship. One left. If you sell it this week the rent is no longer a problem this week. “Hustle the scanner with everything you've got” opens the route to Your Son's Birthday. “Drop it and focus only on the internship” changes the terms and carries you toward Midterm Review.

choices.text: Hustle the scanner with everything you've got
choices.consequence: Old debts don't care about new dreams. You hustle the scanner with everything you've got. The decision moves you toward Your Son's Birthday and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Drop it and focus only on the internship
choices.consequence: Bet on the bigger long game. You commit to drop it and focus only on the internship. By Midterm Review, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: He turns six. You scrape together a small cake and a story and a promise you can't quite keep. He blows out the candles like it's the easiest day of his life. You realize, watching him, that he thinks it is.

choices.text: Tell him about the dream you're chasing
choices.consequence: Children deserve to know the story they're inside. You tell him about the dream you're chasing. The decision moves you toward The Rival and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Just be present for the day
choices.consequence: Some birthdays don't need a speech. You choose to just be present for the day. It opens the route to Sick Day, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Your supervisor pulls you aside and tells you you're in the top two. He pauses. 'You're also,' he says, 'a year behind everyone in the network.' He is, as senior brokers go, kind. “Ask him for one piece of honest advice” draws you toward The Rival; “Thank him and double your efforts” leaves Sick Day waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Ask him for one piece of honest advice
choices.consequence: Mentorship is the only shortcut that's safe. You ask him for one piece of honest advice. The decision moves you toward The Rival and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Thank him and double your efforts
choices.consequence: You choose to thank him and double your efforts. It opens the route to Sick Day, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Another intern — sharper-suited, sharper-tongued — has started taking credit for your accounts. The senior partners can't quite tell. You can. To choose “Call it out in the next meeting” means meeting Week Nineteen; “Beat him on results so loud nobody can mistake them” sends you toward The Final Call instead.

choices.text: Call it out in the next meeting
choices.consequence: Truth aimed cleanly is allowed at work too. You choose to call it out in the next meeting. It opens the route to Week Nineteen, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Beat him on results so loud nobody can mistake them
choices.consequence: Numbers don't lie in this building. You choose to beat him on results so loud nobody can mistake them. It opens the route to The Final Call, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Your son spikes a fever and the daycare can't keep him. You have a 9 a.m. meeting that cannot be missed. The world has, again, asked you for two whole lives. The distance between Week Nineteen and The Final Call begins with the choice between “Bring him to the office, hide him under your desk” and “Skip the meeting and explain truthfully later.”

choices.text: Bring him to the office, hide him under your desk
choices.consequence: Improvise; apologize; survive. You bring him to the office, hide him under your desk. The decision moves you toward Week Nineteen and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Skip the meeting and explain truthfully later
choices.consequence: Honesty is also a strategy. You commit to skip the meeting and explain truthfully later. By The Final Call, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: You've been here long enough that the marble lobby looks ordinary. You look down at your hands and they're a little steadier. So is your son's. Your suit fits, finally. The distance between Friday Morning and Whatever Friday Says begins with the choice between “Walk in tomorrow like you already work here” and “Stay humble; the decision isn't yours.”

choices.text: Walk in tomorrow like you already work here
choices.consequence: Belonging is a posture you adopt before they grant it. You choose to walk in tomorrow like you already work here. It opens the route to Friday Morning, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Stay humble; the decision isn't yours
choices.consequence: Pride is the last thing to lose, and the easiest. You commit to stay humble; the decision isn't yours. By Whatever Friday Says, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: On the second-to-last day you land an account so improbable a senior partner stares at you for a long moment, then quietly hands you his card. 'Whatever happens Friday,' he says, 'call me.' That sentence is worth more than the job.

choices.text: Be ready to take Friday's news either way
choices.consequence: A door, opened, is an option. You commit to be ready to take Friday's news either way. By Friday Morning, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Resolve to take only the offered job, on principle
choices.consequence: Loyalty has its costs and its rewards. You resolve to take only the offered job, on principle. The decision moves you toward Whatever Friday Says and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Your supervisor calls you into his office. There is a single white envelope on the desk. He smiles, just slightly. You realize you have not breathed in approximately a minute. “Open the envelope yourself” opens the route to The Offer. “Let him tell you out loud” changes the terms and carries you toward Whatever Comes Next.

choices.text: Open the envelope yourself
choices.consequence: Take the news in your own hands. You open the envelope yourself. The decision moves you toward The Offer and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Let him tell you out loud
choices.consequence: Some sentences are meant to be spoken. You choose to let him tell you out loud. It opens the route to Whatever Comes Next, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Whatever the envelope says, the truth is already known by the people who've watched you do this — and by your son, who looked at you this morning and said, 'You did it, Dad,' as if it were obvious.

choices.text: Believe him before the envelope speaks
choices.consequence: Some verdicts beat the official ones. You commit to believe him before the envelope speaks. By The Offer, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Wait for the room to call it official
choices.consequence: Hope and proof both have their seats. You commit to wait for the room to call it official. By Whatever Comes Next, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: It's yes. It's the job. There are tears you didn't plan and a handshake you'll remember and a phone call to your sister that you make in a stairwell so nobody sees you cry. None of it feels real. All of it is.

choices.text: Take the job and build the life
choices.consequence: Doors open. Walk through. You commit to take the job and build the life. By Stockbroker, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Take the job — and remember everyone who helped
choices.consequence: Success is not a solo act. You choose to take the job — and remember everyone who helped. It opens the route to The People Who Carried You, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Whether the envelope says yes or no, you walk out of the building taller than you walked in. You learned what you came to learn — that you can take a punch and stand up. The senior partner's card is warm in your pocket.

choices.text: Call the senior partner Monday no matter what
choices.consequence: When the front door closes, knock on a window. You commit to call the senior partner Monday no matter what. By The Other Door, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Take your son out for something silly
choices.consequence: Today is for him. Tomorrow is for everything else. You take your son out for something silly. The decision moves you toward Your Son's Father and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Years later, in a corner office, you find a small plastic rocket in the bottom drawer and laugh and almost cry. The boy who once asked if you had a plan is in college now. You had a plan. You just had to learn it as you went.

You learn fast to send the elevator back down. You hire from shelters, from night classes, from places you knew. The job becomes a door you hold open for someone else. That, you realize, is what pursuit actually means.

You don't get the internship's job. You make the call. The other door opens — smaller, slower, but yours. Some pursuits are not a straight line. Yours is more interesting for the detour. The road into The Other Door began with “Call the senior partner Monday no matter what” in Whatever Comes Next; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

Whatever the job becomes, you become a father who is present, who showed up, who proved a man can be broke and not broken. He grows up steady because you decided to. That is, by any honest measure, the better fortune.
